night.note: The page ground and the only background under running text. Near-neutral with a residual plateau blue (chroma 0.0115 at hue 267), measured from the shipped hex — not chroma zero.

basalt.note: A material token with exactly one use left in the stylesheet: the copy control on a fenced code block inside a chat answer (.bb-copy-btn). It is a chip on a night-ground block, not a container - a lighter square that reads as pressable against the darker code under it. Ink-2 on basalt is 6.3:1. Not a general surface material; the figure scroller and code bodies it used to carry moved to the well.

ink.note: Display and body text. 17.2:1 on night, 17.5:1 on the well, 11.4:1 on ember, and the primary button's hover fill (night on ink, 17.2:1).

ink-2.note: Metadata, muted prose and secondary links. 7.0:1 on night, so it holds AA at any size.

ink-3.note: Container strokes and separators. 3.2:1 on night — not a text colour at body size.

red.note: Adobe Spectrum red-900 (dark theme). The only chromatic accent, and it works in both directions: 5.6:1 as type on night and as a ground under night-coloured type. State and one structural rule; never a surface. It also carries ::selection (night on red, 5.6:1), which used to be the structural fill - which is why selecting text came back sage.

ember.note: The structural fill, in the accent's own hue. Fill only, never text: the code-block header, the markdown table head, the chat error block, the assistant's marker square, the blockquote rule, and the case-study diagram fills. Derived rather than picked - the same OKLCH lightness as the pinyon-juniper sage it replaces, at the red's hue (30) and twice the chroma, because at the sage's chroma that hue reads brown rather than red. Ink on ember 11.4:1, ink-2 on ember 4.6:1, red on ember 3.7:1; 1.5:1 against night, so it reads as a tint of the ground.

ember-lift.note: The lighter structural fill: the assistant marker, the blockquote rule, the chat error border and the diagram strokes. Ink on it measures 8.6:1.

well.note: One step below night, and the ground for every container that holds its own content: the chat frame, the expanded chat sheet, the case-study figure scroller and case-study code blocks. Same blue family as night and inside the same near-neutral band, and every text ratio against it is higher than against night: ink 17.5:1, ink-2 7.1:1, red 5.7:1, ink-3 3.2:1. Figures and code moved here from basalt and every value improved - node stroke 2.86:1 -> 3.22:1 (clearing the 3:1 floor for a UI boundary), labels 15.6:1 -> 17.5:1, sub-labels 6.3:1 -> 7.1:1, code ink 15.6:1 -> 17.5:1, the red 5.1:1 -> 5.7:1, the string colour 8.8:1 -> 9.9:1.

dot.note: 10% ink, painted as a 1px radial-gradient on a 22px pitch (--dot-gap) over the well, on the chat surfaces only - figures and code blocks take the well without it. A dot composites to #1D1E22, 1.2:1 against the well - texture, not an edge. Measured by hand against a dot: ink 14.5:1, ink-2 5.9:1, red 4.7:1, ink-3 2.7:1 (under the 3:1 floor). The contrast harness reads background-color only and cannot see it.

hair.note: 14% ink over the ground. Structural dividers, section tops, resting row borders.

hair-strong.note: 26% ink. Emphasis hairlines, hovered row borders, the chat input box, the maturity chip stroke.

display.purpose: The masthead name, uppercase, at width stop 110. Nothing else uses it.

display-long.purpose: The case-study title, one stop smaller so a long name still sets on two lines.

lead.purpose: Featured project names in the work list, at width stop 104.

headline.purpose: Section heads on the home page.

title.purpose: Role names in the record; also the chat markdown h1/h2 via aliases.

lede.purpose: Masthead subhead, case-study one-liner, colophon and section openers. Capped at 48-58ch with opsz 24.

body.purpose: Running prose in Archivo, a sans, to a 65ch measure. Not a serif: the earlier Literata body is gone from this build.

body-small.purpose: Descriptors, role descriptions, list rows and chat answers.

ui.purpose: Values in meta lists, footnotes, figure captions, back links.

label.purpose: Every stamp, key and chip: 11px uppercase, 0.1em, width stop 88, tabular numerals.

code.purpose: JetBrains Mono, confined to code blocks, paths, timestamps, source chips and the MCP endpoint.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one loud action: red fill, night text, square, uppercase at the metadata width stop. Shares one box with the ghost - inline-flex, centred, min-height 48px, padding 13px 24px.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The secondary action, and the shape a disabled control falls back to rather than dimming a bright fill. Same box as the primary; ink text so it reads as live rather than disabled beside a solid fill.

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Metadata as a bordered chip. The active variant inverts to a red fill, the only place a chip is loud.

components.name: Grid Toggle
components.description: The signature control. Carries a four-bar mark of the twelve-column overlay it turns on, and inverts to red when pressed.

components.description: Field and send button inside one hairline box; the box takes focus-within so the composed control lights as a single object.

narrative.overview:
The page is a black field with very large type on it. One grotesque - Archivo - carries display, heading, UI and body alike, at a single weight, and rank is expressed by size, by width on the variable font’s wdth axis, and by which column a thing occupies. There is no second family in the reading band, no case change inside prose, no shadow, no gradient, no rounded corner, and no accent but one red.

The page is fluid: --shell is 100% and the gutter is the margin, so the edge of the viewport is the edge of the sheet at every width. Fluidity has one cost - a row composed on twelve columns at 2560px puts a name at one edge and its action at the other - and the system pays it with --row-max: 1240px on the composed rows, the content width at 1440 where the composition was measured. The masthead is exempt on purpose.

Beneath that sits a twelve-column grid. Three regions are composed on it - lead rows, role rows and section heads - adopting it at 900px and collapsing to one column below. The grid overlay draws those columns as red hairlines on demand. It is the signature element and it is functional rather than decorative: a reader gets to check the structure instead of taking it on faith.
keyCharacteristics: One face, one weight (500), four widths; size and width are the whole hierarchy.
Radius 0 everywhere; hairlines and fills instead of shadows.
Fluid page, capped rows (1240px), twelve columns revealed on demand.
One accent hue at two lightnesses: a signal red for state and one structural rule, a deep ember that fills.
Motion is state transition only: 120ms and 220ms on one ease-out-quart curve.

rules.name: The Chroma Discipline Rule
rules.body: Neutrals are near-neutral and stay there: night, basalt and the ink ramp all measure below 0.013 OKLCH chroma (night C 0.0115 at hue 267, basalt C 0.0129, ink C 0.0041). That residual is the plateau’s blue sky in the ground, not warmth - no beige, no brown, no touch of warmth in the near-black, and no neutral that reads as a hue. Measured from the shipped hexes; a repo note elsewhere states these are at chroma exactly 0, and the artifact does not support that figure.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: There is one chromatic hue in the system and it appears at two lightnesses: red signals, ember fills. Red marks state or a single structural rule and is never a surface; ember is never text. Nothing else is coloured - a second hue is what the sage was, and removing it is what made the palette one voice instead of two.

rules.name: The Unmeasurable Texture Rule
rules.body: The contrast harness reads each element's resolved background-color and cannot see a background-image, so on the dotted well it reports the well every time and never measures a dot. Measured by hand, text sitting directly on a dot: ink 14.5:1, ink-2 5.9:1, red 4.7:1 - and --ink-3 2.7:1, under the 3:1 floor. The chat renders only ink and ink-2 today, so nothing fails; --ink-3 on the dotted well is the one combination in this system that passes the automated audit and fails the eye. Any new patterned ground inherits this: measure the composite by hand, because the audit will not.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every contrast figure in this document was measured against rendered sRGB, never reasoned from OKLCH lightness - OKLCH lightness is perceptual and estimating ratios from it produces wrong answers. Re-measure the whole table after any palette change. The audited state: 438 text elements across / and /work/felix at 1440 and 390, none below WCAG AA.

rules.name: The Width Ladder Rule
rules.body: Archivo’s wdth axis encodes rank, and there are exactly four stops: 110% display, 104% heading, 100% UI, 88% metadata. No fifth value, no interpolation. The ladder only exists if the Fontsource wdth entrypoint is imported (@fontsource-variable/archivo/wdth.css); import wght instead and every font-stretch in the sheet silently does nothing while the build stays green.

rules.name: The 1.15x Rule
rules.body: Adjacent stops on the type ramp are at least 1.15x apart. Two stops closer than that are two names for one role; collapse the newer one onto the existing stop as an alias.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: 500 for everything, 700 only for <strong>, which is semantic rather than hierarchical. Weight never carries rank - width and size do.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: No shadow, no gradient, no radius, no glow. If something needs to separate from what is behind it, give it a hairline, a different material (the well or ember), or more space - never a lift.

rules.name: The Motion Budget Rule
rules.body: Motion is state transition only: 120ms and 220ms on cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1). No scroll choreography, no entrance animation, nothing that gates content on an animation finishing. prefers-reduced-motion reduces everything to 0.01ms.

rules.name: The Contained Content Rule
rules.body: A container that holds its own content rather than carrying the page's - the conversation, a diagram, a code block - sits in --well on a 1px --ink-3 stroke. One ground for all three is one fewer material to justify, and it is the darkest ground in the system, so every token gains contrast on the way in.

dos: Do set body copy in Archivo (`--font-body`, which aliases `--font-display`) at 500, 20px, 1.6, to a 65ch measure.
Do pick one of the four width stops — 110 / 104 / 100 / 88 — for anything new, and import `@fontsource-variable/archivo/wdth.css` or the stops do not exist.
Do express hierarchy with size, width and column position, in that order.
Do compose new rows on the twelve columns with metadata in 1–2, content in 3–9, action in 11–12, and cap them at `--row-max` (1240px).
Do use `--hair` (14%) for structure and `--hair-strong` (26%) for emphasis and resting interactive borders; those are the only two hairline weights.
Do keep type on night, the well or ember only; ink on all three measures 11:1 or better. Basalt carries one 11px label (the copy chip) and is not a surface for prose.
Do re-measure contrast against the rendered DOM after any palette change, and re-measure the Archivo/Helvetica metrics if the font package or the weight moves.
Do set every stamp, key and chip at the 11px label stop, uppercase, `0.1em`, tabular numerals.
Do put any container that holds its own content — conversation, diagram, code — on `--well` with a 1px `--ink-3` stroke, and add the dot grid only on the chat surfaces.
Do give `.btn` and `.btn-ghost` the same box: `inline-flex`, centred, `min-height: 48px`, `padding: 13px 24px`. Agreement is declared, not inherited from whatever row happens to hold them.
Do re-declare `color` inside any rule that changes a control's background on hover.
Do name the action in a control's label — the mailto button reads "Email me", not "Talk to me".
Do keep tokens in the stylesheet; a renamed token must break visibly in one place rather than silently in five inline styles.
donts: Don't introduce a serif, a second sans, or any third family. Mono is JetBrains Mono and is confined to code, paths, timestamps and readouts.
Don't warm the neutrals or push any neutral above ~0.013 OKLCH chroma. The residual blue in night is the world; beige is not.
Don't add a second accent hue. Red signals, ember fills, and they are one hue at two lightnesses; nothing else is coloured.
Don't set text on ember below large size — red on ember measures 3.7:1 — and don't set body-size text in `--ink-3` (3.2:1 on night); it is a border and decoration value.
Don't add a radius, a shadow, a gradient or a decorative blur. If separation is needed, use a hairline, a different material, or space.
Don't add a type stop within 1.15x of an existing one; alias onto the existing stop instead.
Don't use weight for hierarchy. 700 belongs to `<strong>` and nowhere else.
Don't put the masthead's red rule inside a column, and don't cap the masthead at `--row-max`; it is exempt on purpose.
Don't add scroll-triggered animation, entrance reveals, or any motion outside the 120ms/220ms state-transition budget.

Don't put `--ink-3` text — or any new colour — on the dotted well without measuring it against a dot by hand. Ink-3 on a dot is 2.7:1, under the 3:1 floor, and the contrast harness cannot see a `background-image`, so it will report the well and pass.
Don't cap the expanded chat at a fixed card width; it is `100%` x `100dvh` on purpose, because a fluid inline frame outgrows any cap.
Don't let `.bb-shell` become a scroll container; it clips on x only, or the sticky top bar stops sticking.

Don't change a button's hover background without re-declaring its `color` in the same rule. The global `a:hover { color: var(--red) }` outranks `.btn`, which only declares its colour at rest: when the primary's hover became an `--ink` fill, the label went red on near-white at 3.05:1, a real failure that the old transparent hover had hidden (red on night is 5.64:1). The automated contrast harness will not catch this — it measures the resting state only.

Don't move the figure ground without moving the diagram node default with it. `.bb-figure-scroll` is `--well` and `Box` in `app/content/case-studies.tsx` defaults `fill = 'var(--well)'` so an ordinary node sits flush and reads by its stroke; if the ground changes and the default does not, every unfilled node grows a panel behind it.

Don't treat `--basalt` as a surface material. It has exactly one use in the stylesheet — the copy chip on a chat code block — and reaching for it as a panel ground undoes the recession that makes containers read.

Don't set a case-study `<strong>` at `--wt`. It is identical to its parent and cancels the browser's bold, which made every term in a term/detail list invisible; `--wt-strong` (700) is what that second weight is for.
Don't leave a case-study block uncapped. Hero and body children take `--row-max` on the child, not on the centred wrapper, or the page grows a second and third right edge at wide viewports.
Don't reintroduce kickers or eyebrows above headings. The masthead subhead opens with the job title verbatim instead, and nothing in the build uses one.
